---
title: "Link functions"
execute:
  warning: false
  message: false
---

A [**link function**](https://appliedstatisticsforlinguists.org/bwinter_stats_proofs.pdf#page=214) maps a constrained conditional mean to the real-valued linear predictor. We continue with SuperTelicity, where the response is an *in* choice and the first-use source and design are introduced on the [preceding page](why-generalized-linear-models.qmd).

This page addresses the **link-choice problem**. A valid link must be one-to-one on the mean space, but the support of that space does not select a unique link. For a Bernoulli mean, the logit, probit, and complementary log-log links are all valid. They instead encode different assumptions about how a real-valued predictor approaches zero and one.

```{r}
#| label: load-and-fit-link
#| echo: true
st <- read.csv("data/supertelicity/supertelicity-cloze.csv")
st$verb_type <- factor(st$verb_type, levels = c("manner", "result"))
st$duration_centered <- st$log_duration_minutes -
  mean(st$log_duration_minutes, na.rm = TRUE)
st <- st[!is.na(st$duration_centered), ]
fit <- glm(prep_in ~ duration_centered + verb_type,
           family = binomial(link = "logit"), data = st)
```

For a Bernoulli mean $0<\pi_i<1$, the logit link and its inverse are

$$
g(\pi_i)=\log\frac{\pi_i}{1-\pi_i}=\eta_i,
\qquad
g^{-1}(\eta_i)=\frac{1}{1+e^{-\eta_i}}=\pi_i.
$$

The inverse follows by exponentiating: $e^{\eta}=\pi/(1-\pi)$, so $e^\eta(1-\pi)=\pi$ and hence $\pi=e^\eta/(1+e^\eta)$. The logit is especially convenient because a coefficient is a log odds ratio. The probit instead uses $\Phi^{-1}(\pi)$, whereas the complementary log-log link $\log[-\log(1-\pi)]$ is asymmetric.

```{r}
#| label: compare-valid-bernoulli-links
#| echo: true
p <- sort(unique(aggregate(prep_in ~ verb_type, st, mean)$prep_in))
data.frame(probability = p, logit = qlogis(p), probit = qnorm(p),
           complementary_log_log = log(-log(1 - p)))
```

The link acts on the conditional mean, not on the observed zeros and ones. The fitted SuperTelicity model supplies actual values on both scales.

```{r}
#| label: link-map
#| echo: true
observed <- aggregate(prep_in ~ verb_type, st, mean)
observed$empirical_logit <- qlogis(observed$prep_in)
observed$round_trip_probability <- plogis(observed$empirical_logit)
observed
```

`qlogis()` maps the empirical group probabilities to real numbers, and `plogis()` returns them to the probability scale. These functions implement the equations above without transforming any response row.

## The inverse link keeps predictions valid

```{r}
#| label: plot-link-fit
#| echo: true
library(ggplot2)
grid <- expand.grid(
  duration_centered = seq(min(st$duration_centered), max(st$duration_centered),
                          length.out = 201L),
  verb_type = levels(st$verb_type)
)
grid$log_duration_minutes <- grid$duration_centered + mean(st$log_duration_minutes)
grid$eta <- predict(fit, newdata = grid, type = "link")
grid$probability <- plogis(grid$eta)
st$duration_bin <- cut(st$log_duration_minutes,
  unique(quantile(st$log_duration_minutes, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = 13L))),
  include.lowest = TRUE)
binned <- aggregate(cbind(prep_in, log_duration_minutes) ~ duration_bin + verb_type,
                    st, mean)
ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = binned,
             aes(log_duration_minutes, prep_in, shape = verb_type), size = 1.7) +
  geom_line(data = grid,
            aes(log_duration_minutes, probability, linetype = verb_type),
            color = "#1F5A85", linewidth = .8) +
  labs(x = "Selected duration (log minutes)",
       y = "Probability of an in-completion", shape = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  theme_classic()
```

The model is additive in $\eta_i$ but curved in $\pi_i$. A constant coefficient is a constant change in log odds, not in probability. The link changes neither the Bernoulli support nor the observed response. It connects the linear predictor to the family mean.

For instance, the same one-unit logit coefficient has different response-scale consequences at different baselines.

```{r}
#| label: baseline-dependent-probability-change
#| echo: true
baseline <- observed$prep_in
data.frame(baseline,
  after_one_log_odds_unit = plogis(qlogis(baseline) + 1),
  probability_change = plogis(qlogis(baseline) + 1) - baseline)
```

For count means the analogous construction uses $\log\lambda_i=\eta_i$ and $\lambda_i=e^{\eta_i}>0$. Thus support constrains a link choice, but it does not determine that choice. A link is not a device for making a histogram look normal.

## Recap and check

1. Does a Bernoulli response force the logit link? No. It forces predicted means into $(0,1)$; scientific and computational considerations distinguish valid links.
2. If a logit coefficient is one, is the probability change one? No. The coefficient is a one-unit log odds change, and the corresponding probability change depends on the baseline.

The [GLM template](generalized-linear-models.qmd) next keeps the response distribution, linear predictor, and link separate.
